head: diag-pending-pings-delivered-read-surface
title: diag: give the ping delivery ledger a read surface
body:
## Summary

`scripts/notify_on_pull.py` records the sha256 of every `docs/claude/pending-pings.jsonl` line it enqueues into `runtime_logs/pending_pings_delivered.txt`, and that file was on **no read surface**. This adds it to `_LOG_FILES` in `src/web/api/routers/diag.py`, together with the `CLAUDE.md` `log_file` row in the **same commit** (the `exit_loop_health` #8778 rule).

Measured live against the **running** web-api process, not just source: `/api/diag/log_file?name=pending_pings_delivered` → `unknown_log_file`, with 45 allowlisted names and **0** ping/notify/delivery related. Positive controls `exit_loop_health`, `stray_oca_soak`, `pairs_soak` all resolve, so the extraction is sound and the negative has a denominator.

So *"the operator's work digest was delivered"* and *"the drain never ran"* were **indistinguishable from outside** — the recurring `BL-20260825-ALERT-AND-CADENCE-STATE-FILES-SHIP-WITHOUT-A-READ-SURFACE` shape, and at least its fifth instance.

### ⚠️ The entry is anchored to `repo_root()`, not `runtime_logs_dir()` — deliberately

The naive entry would have been **wrong**, and wrong in the direction that reads as an answer:

| | resolves to |
|---|---|
| naive — `runtime_logs_dir() / "pending_pings_delivered.txt"` | `/data/bot-data/runtime_logs/pending_pings_delivered.txt` |
| **shipped** — `Path(repo_root()) / "runtime_logs" / ...` | `/home/ubuntu/ict-trading-bot/runtime_logs/pending_pings_delivered.txt` |

`notify_on_pull.py` hardcodes its own `REPO_ROOT / "runtime_logs"` and never calls the path helpers. It runs from `ict-git-sync.service`, which carries **no** data-dir drop-in. This reader runs in `ict-web-api.service`, which **does** carry `deploy/dropins/data-dir.conf` (`Environment=DATA_DIR=/data/bot-data`).

Verified live rather than reasoned: `?name=exit_loop_health` reports `"path":"/data/bot-data/runtime_logs/exit_loop_health.json"`.

Routing this entry through the helper would have pointed the read surface at a path **nothing writes** and served a permanently-absent file — which a reader would take as *"nothing was ever delivered"*. That is the writer/reader path split that hid the `ict-hourly-snapshot` balance stall for ~3 weeks (`BL-20260611-M15-2`), reproduced on the one surface built to detect it.

I did **not** "fix" this by moving the writer to the helper. Moving the ledger empties it, and an empty ledger means every one of the 50 lines in `pending-pings.jsonl` re-fires on the next pull — a ping storm at the operator, from an observability PR. Reader follows writer; the divergence is reported below instead.

## Architecture impact

- [x] **Not applicable** — one entry on an existing read-only, token-gated diag route plus its mandatory doc row. No schema, boundary, pipeline, deployment, contract, or config change.

## Test plan

- [x] `tests/test_diag_log_file_allowlist_coherence.py` — 5 passed. Both directions pinned: 46 names in code, 46 in the doc, symmetric difference empty each way.
- [x] Positive control on the probe itself — confirmed `_code_names()` and `_documented_names()` each actually **contain** `pending_pings_delivered`, so the pass is not vacuous.
- [x] `tests/test_web_api_diag.py` — 30 passed.
- [x] `tests/test_diag_exit_loop_health_reachable.py`, `test_diag_version_reports_running_sha.py` — 13 passed with the above.
- [x] Path resolution asserted under the VM's real `DATA_DIR=/data/bot-data`, showing the naive and shipped forms diverge (table above).
- [x] `scripts/ci/run_guards.py --pr-diff` on the **committed** diff: **PASS 48 · FAIL 1 · SKIP 18**; the single fail was `layer-guard` `exited 127` (`lint-imports` absent from the runner). Installed it and ran it directly — **6 contracts kept, 0 broken** — because this PR adds an import (`repo_root`) and layer-guard is genuinely in scope for it. Effective: **49/49**.
- [ ] CI green

## What this unblocks, and the honest state of it

The question this exists to answer: **was the `2026-09-02T00:19:53Z` `work_digest` line actually delivered to `@ict_cluade_bot`?**

The lookup key is settled — I read `_line_hash` rather than guessing, and it hashes the **raw stripped jsonl line**, not the parsed payload:

```
line 50 of docs/claude/pending-pings.jsonl  (1370 bytes)
sha256 = 8ccf385180c770542d39a2f8325a31ae2e5a55552c22cb68b9fdd1d0b1c1b263
```

Current answer: **`could_not_look`** — a distinct state from `not_delivered`, and it stays that way until this merges, deploys, **and the web-api restarts**. A ledger nobody can read is not evidence of non-delivery. I am not reporting a verdict I do not have.

## Filed for follow-ups

Reported here rather than filed — backlog files are out of scope for this session and siblings are draining them.

1. **`notify_on_pull.py` bypasses the path helpers.** It hardcodes `REPO_ROOT / "runtime_logs"` while every other consumer resolves through `runtime_logs_dir()`. Today that is *load-bearing* — `ict-git-sync.service` has no data-dir drop-in, so the hardcode is the only reason writer and reader agree at all. But it means the ledger silently lives outside `DATA_DIR`: it is not on the block volume, not backed up with it, and **a re-provision or re-clone resets it**, which re-fires every retained line. Worth a decision, not a drive-by fix.

2. **`pending-pings.jsonl` is append-only and never truncated** (rows from 2026-07-06 are still present; 50 lines). The dedupe ledger is now the *only* thing preventing a full replay, and until this PR it was unreadable — so the mechanism guarding against a 50-ping storm had no health surface at all.

3. **`/api/diag/version` currently reports `restart_pending: true`** — `git_sha` (running) `49f03e37`, `git_sha_on_disk` `7187ffde`. Disk is ahead of the running process right now. This does not affect ping delivery (the drain runs in `ict-git-sync.service` at pull time, not in the web-api), but it does gate when *this* PR's read surface becomes usable.

## Corrections to the brief I was given

Both are corrections to *evidence*, not refutations of the conclusions.

- **The VM-has-pulled-past-it claim cited the wrong field.** The brief quoted `git_sha_on_disk: de61ead9`. `git_sha_on_disk` is the **disk** sha; `git_sha` is the running one, and `diag.py`'s own comment says this endpoint was rebuilt specifically because reading disk cannot answer "did the restart roll the code forward". The value is also stale now. Re-measured: running `49f03e37`, disk `7187ffde`. **The conclusion survives** — `d74e0b2c` *is* an ancestor of the running `49f03e37` (verified with `git merge-base --is-ancestor`), so the VM genuinely is past the digest commit.

- **`OI-20260901-SCHEDULED-PROBES-AND-DUE-LIST-HAVE-NEVER-FIRED-ON-CRON` is untouched.** That row's population is `probes.yml` and `due-list.yml`. `work-digest.yml` firing on `schedule` is a *different* workflow — new evidence about cron in this repo, **not** a refutation of that row. It should not be closed on the strength of it.
